items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You know actually I was in a colleague of yours, Dave Rivello’s music room...

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Oh yeah, just riding in the car or something you know, thinking of a bass line or something like that. I know people that try to write them down as soon as they can, they just have a little notebook of — in fact I kept a notebook for a long time just called “Ideas” and I’d just write stuff down where you know it could be a big band chart on so- and-so and stuff like that. And then I’d come back to that and look at it say oh yeah that could work and then I’d go ahead and sketch it out and go from there.

You obviously were in the era of using score pads and I’m wondering if you transitioned to Finale or Sibelius? You know actually I was in a colleague of yours, Dave Rivello’s music room and I was pleasantly surprised to see this big table with a huge pad on it and pencils. And he insisted it was important to do the physical act of putting a note on a piece of paper.

Uh huh, yeah. Well I do it both ways. I sketch stuff and figure out things on the piano, and then I use Finale also and you know, put it in. And I got pretty good on Finale and pretty fast, like because every summer I’d go to Germany and I was in charge of the Eastman Philharmonia, they had a gig there playing in Heidelberg at a castle there. And I didn’t have a piano so I had just the computer. And I edited a whole bunch of books and stuff, and I did a lot of editing for my publisher, Advance Music. And so I got…
